title: I finally made my first game. Sharing it was scary; thinking about Steam is even scarier.
author: abner-ruza
selftext:
Hey everyone!

Yesterday I released another game I’d been working on, and it was really well received. That gave me the confidence to share **CytoSquad** with you too.

Making a game has been a dream of mine, and now there’s actually something people can download and play. That alone feels like a huge personal milestone.

CytoSquad is an action survival roguelite set inside the human body. You play as an immune cell fighting viruses, bacteria, and bosses, either solo or with up to 4 players in online co-op. I’m building it in Godot with AI assistance.

**The playable beta is available now for FREE on Windows:**  
[Check out CytoSquad on itch.io](https://rzatech.itch.io/cytosquad)

I really want to bring it to Steam eventually, but honestly, I’m scared it’ll flop. Yesterday’s encouragement helped, but I’d also love honest, specific feedback that can help me improve it.

* Does the concept make you want to try it?
* If you play, what feels fun, confusing, or frustrating?
* What would you want improved before a Steam release?

Even a few thoughts would mean a lot. Finishing and sharing my first game is a dream come true, and I want to keep making it better.
